title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial (N=150 synthetic intents; paired baseline vs guarded; shared_initial_candidate semantics) to test whether constrained prompting plus deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair) increases semantic correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level network configuration sequences. Model: gpt-5-mini; verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Primary outcome: verifier pass/fail per intent. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.33%), guarded = 150/150 (100.0%), paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (0.67 percentage points), exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150). Interpretation: on this synthetic corpus the guarded workflow produced no statistically or practically meaningful improvement over a near-ceiling baseline; this illustrates a ceiling effect and underscores the need to calibrate preregistered power assumptions to realistic baseline competence. Claims are explicitly bounded to the archived synthetic corpus, single model, and deterministic validator used.

sections.introduction: Natural-language intent interfaces aim to make network operations more accessible by translating operator intent into concrete low-level configuration sequences. Prior work reports that LLMs can produce useful configuration templates yet can make syntactic or semantic errors that require downstream correction [1], and that verifier-guided generate→verify→repair pipelines can reduce such errors for infrastructure artifacts [2], [3]. Agentic tool-using pipelines further motivate deterministic validation because of claim-to-action vulnerabilities [4]. We therefore preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment to answer the research question: Does combining constrained prompting (structured templates + explicit semantic slots) with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation compared to an unconstrained baseline? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, paired confirmatory design focused on verifier verdicts; (2) a complete archived execution (N=150 paired tasks, model = gpt-5-mini, verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5); and (3) an empirical, artifact-grounded result that bounds the marginal benefit of a single-repair guarded pipeline on a synthetic corpus that produced a near-ceiling baseline.
sections.related_work: Three strands informed the experiment. Intent-to-configuration and NL→formal-spec studies document modest semantic-correctness in many benchmarked settings and the difficulty of producing verifier-sound specifications from free text [1]. Verifier-aware generation and iterative repair have improved correctness for IaC and configuration tasks when paired with deterministic or policy-guided verifiers [2], [6]. Security analyses show agentic pipelines can convert textual claims into harmful actions and motivate verifier gating and auditable controls [4], [5]. Mature verification tools (e.g., NetKAT/KATch and related systems) provide deterministic oracles suitable for reachability, isolation, and policy checks and therefore support verifier-level outcome measurement [3]. Our study situates a preregistered paired trial at the intersection of these strands and measures verifier pass/fail as the primary outcome.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and frozen prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256 = aea996afce45e3798345f6e32ae6c347456f103ecdb84fc36e27bb486a329399). Design: a paired binary comparison between (A) baseline free-text prompt and (C) constrained-template prompt plus deterministic verifier-guided single-repair attempt (guarded). The preregistration also conceptually specified a constrained-only condition (B), but the executed adapter and confirmatory run implemented only the paired baseline vs guarded episodes under shared_initial_candidate semantics; condition B was not executed and secondary contrasts involving B are therefore not reported. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract: for each intent a single initial model generation served as the common initial candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call triggered deterministically by the verifier. Model and verifier: declared model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (literal recorded value). We report that temperature was recorded as null/unset in the archive; null does not imply we claim deterministic sampling (no claim of temperature=0 or determinism is made). Sampling metadata were recorded for every model call. Planned sample and budget: N=150 distinct synthetic intents (paired episodes = 300), at most one initial model call per task and at most one repair call per task. Stopping and exclusion rules: ambiguity detection and parser/coverage exclusions were applied deterministically prior to model calls; none were excluded during the run. Analysis plan: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; exact McNemar two-sided test for the paired binary contrast; 95% bootstrap percentile CIs computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All mapping code, model-call logs, verifier inputs and verdicts, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned paired episodes = 300; completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations observed = 1. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0066666667 (0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the difference = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Repair diagnostics: only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150); median revision iterations in guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Missingness/exclusions/contamination: none observed. Interpretation of shared_initial_candidate semantics: the baseline rate reports the verifier pass/fail on the single initial generation per intent; the guarded rate reports the final verifier verdict after the guarded pipeline completed (post-repair where invoked). Because initial candidates were overwhelmingly valid (149/150), the guarded pipeline had a single opportunity to convert a failing initial candidate and did so once.
sections.discussion: Summary: constrained prompting plus a deterministic verifier-guided single-repair produced no material improvement over an already high-performing baseline on this preregistered synthetic corpus. This outcome reflects a ceiling effect rather than a general refutation of verifier-guided methods; prior work shows larger gains where baselines are weaker or tasks are more diverse [2], [3]. Methodological implication: preregistered confirmatory trials must calibrate baseline competence (via pilots) to avoid mismatched power assumptions that render planned contrasts uninformative. Operational implication: when base-model correctness is near 100% on representative tasks, single-repair guarded pipelines yield marginal marginal returns but still provide auditability and auditable gating. Design note: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate the marginal effect of the guarded repair step given a common initial candidate; alternative semantics (independent initial samples) or larger repair budgets could change practical outcomes. Relation to prior work: our bounded null result is consistent with reports that verifier guidance helps on harder benchmarks [2], [6] but that gains shrink on easier corpora. Statistical note: the preregistered power calculation assumed a much lower baseline and 15 percentage-point detectible effect; the observed near-ceiling baseline invalidated that calibration and explains the null confirmatory result.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial measuring verifier-level semantic correctness for NL→configuration translation using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic network validator. On the archived synthetic corpus the constrained prompting plus verifier-guided single-repair workflow increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (0.67 percentage points), a numerically small and statistically non-significant change under the preregistered test (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific outcome is methodological: preregistered LLM-for-NetOps trials must carefully calibrate baseline competence to avoid ceiling effects that mask potential benefits of verifier-guided repair. Technically, this result bounds the benefit on the provided synthetic corpus, single model, and deterministic verifier; it does not contradict prior findings that verifier guidance can materially help on more challenging, diverse, or adversarially designed tasks.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned effect size 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures verifier pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim full operational safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
